note: The geographical Amur/Amour dictionary sense is irrelevant to a French learner entry. The core word is amour = love/affection.
Ouvrir primarily means open; 'turn on/switch on' is not a safe general equivalent for devices. It can also begin/open a session or access.
proposed_english: to open; to begin/start; to open up; to access

note: 'Famous' is not a normal standalone gloss for gros. Core senses are big/large, thick, fat, coarse, and major/important in context.
proposed_english: big; large; thick; fat; coarse; major/important (context-dependent)

note: Porte is not only the noun 'door'; the same written form is also the present-tense verb form 'carries/wears' from porter, a very common learner reading.
proposed_english: door; carries; wears (verb form of porter, context-dependent)

note: The same written form is also the common plural noun sous meaning money/cash; both Larousse and the Académie française explicitly record the plural familiar sense 'argent'.
proposed_english: under; below; beneath; money/cash (plural noun of sou, informal)

note: Type also commonly means guy/man/person informally, not only type/kind/category.
The entry should explicitly mark register: foutre is vulgar and has broad colloquial uses beyond a literal English 'fuck/screw'.
proposed_english: to fuck; to put/do/throw (vulgar, highly context-dependent); semen (dated/vulgar noun)

note: Droit is a major multifunction word: adjective 'right/straight/upright', adverb 'straight', and noun 'right/entitlement; law'. The current gloss omits the ordinary adjective/adverb meanings.
proposed_english: right; straight; upright; straight ahead; right/entitlement; law

note: Putain is vulgar and functions not only as a noun but very commonly as an interjection/intensifier. Register and POS must be explicit.
Jeune also functions as a noun meaning a young person/youth; noun POS is present but the noun meaning is missing.
The intransitive 'escape/run away' sense normally appears as se sauver; bare sauver means save/rescue. The entry should distinguish this.
proposed_english: to save; to rescue; to escape/run away (se sauver)

note: Train also appears in the essential construction être en train de ('to be in the process of') and can mean pace/course/process; noun-only 'train' is too narrow for a high-frequency learner item.
proposed_english: train; pace/course; process (être en train de = to be in the process of)

note: Bare asseoir is transitive ('seat; set/establish'); 'sit down' is normally s'asseoir. The current gloss conflates the two.
proposed_english: to seat; to set/establish; to sit down (s'asseoir)
